references.text: In Ezekiel 37:12-14, the prophet speaks of opening graves and bringing people up from them, a direct parallel to Jesus' words that He will raise up the one who eats His flesh on the last day.
John 11:25-26 confirms Jesus as the resurrection and the life, stating that whoever lives and believes in Him will never die forever, which is the core of the promise in John 6:54.
John 5:24-29 links faith in Jesus to eternal life and a future resurrection on the last day, a theme explicitly repeated in John 6:54.
John 6:40 expresses God's will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes shall have eternal life and be raised up on the last day, a direct precursor to verse 54.
John 6:51 introduces the theme of Jesus as the living bread, where His flesh is given for the life of the world, leading directly to the promise of eternal life in verse 54.
1 Corinthians 15:22-23 discusses how those who belong to Christ will be made alive at His coming, a concept that corresponds with the resurrection on the last day in John 6:54.
